dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/19/Text/1] Among the 23 children who had CDI scores higher than 15 at Time 1, 13 children (56.5%) continued to score higher than 15 at Time 3. (Fifteen was one standard deviation above mean CDI score in Times 1, 2, and 3; 15 is also the cutoff score commonly recommended for designating moderate levels of depression in children.)

Source.evidence_source: [/page/18/Text/10] First, children's CDI scores were highly correlated across the 8-month period. The stability correlations between CDI scores across Times 1, 2, and 3 are presented in Table 7.
